title: Server-Side Rendering
body:
The server builds the finished HTML and sends it already assembled, so the browser can paint meaningful content on the very first response, before any application JavaScript has run. The plate arrives already plated. Classic server frameworks always worked this way — [[Ruby on Rails]] views, PHP templates — and modern frameworks (Next.js, Remix) do it and then "hydrate" the page with JS afterwards to make it interactive.

The work happens on **their machine**, before the response reaches you. Faster first paint and reliable indexing are the wins; the costs are server CPU per request and a page that may look ready before it's actually interactive. The choice between this and [[Client-Side Rendering]] is a textbook example of the "which machine should this run on?" question that the whole [[Web Interview Prep]] set is organised around.
